clue.text: Sweet product from Slough millions say yes to

parts.note: a slough is a bog or swamp, which is a marsh
to say yes to something is to allow it

explanation.surface: A sweet manufactured in the town of Slough wins approval from millions of people.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the English town, but here it is the common noun meaning a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft spongy confection made from sugar and gelatine is a familiar sweet.

clue.text: Reckon D notice comes first

indicators.note: says the notice is placed ahead of the letter D in the answer

parts.note: an advertisement is a notice, shortened to ad

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a government D-notice should take priority.
explanation.walkthrough: A D-notice is a British government request to the press not to publish something; here D and notice split apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon is to calculate, which is to sum figures up.

clue.text: Aggressive speaker submerged in the river

indicators.note: the word for submerged sits inside the letters for 'the river'

parts.note: taken as written
something submerged is under the water

explanation.surface: A loud, aggressive speaker is found drowned in the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who thunders is a loud, aggressive orator; the word was also an old nickname for The Times.

clue.text: Society caring for insect population?

parts.note: a warm person is caring and kind

explanation.surface: A society is caring for a population of insects.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flying mass of bees or other insects is the example the question mark flags.

clue.text: Sea snake one in container for liquid

indicators.note: the snake and the one go inside the container

parts.note: a can holds drinks or other liquids
an asp is a venomous snake
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sea snake has been put into a jar of liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea snake' reads as one creature, but Sea is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the large inland salt lake between Europe and Asia, called a sea.

clue.text: Warm up chicken for ignoramus

parts.note: to warm something up is to heat it
a hen is a chicken

explanation.surface: Only a fool would just warm up leftover chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: An unenlightened or uncivilised person can be called this, extending its religious sense of unbeliever.

clue.text: Long time before noon

indicators.note: places the time ahead of the letter for noon

parts.note: a year is a period of time

explanation.surface: It feels like a long time before noon arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long time' looks like one phrase, but Long is the verb meaning to desire.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to crave or desire it deeply, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Accommodation that brings Masons closer to Craft?

parts.note: Freemasons belong to lodges, so they are lodge men

indicators.note: the closer of a word is its final letter, taken from Craft

explanation.surface: Freemasons find a place to stay that ties them more closely to their order.
explanation.walkthrough: Freemasonry calls itself the Craft, which makes the surface look like a whole-clue riddle; 'that brings' simply joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A place to stay, or the act of lodging, is the older meaning of this word.

clue.text: One often turns to free food — loaf starter?

definitions.text: One often turns to free food — loaf starter?

parts.words: One often turns to free food — loaf starter?
parts.note: a kitchen gadget is turned around a can to release its contents, and it gets things going for an idle person

explanation.surface: A lazy person often turns to free meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaf' is a lazy person, and the gadget is what starts their effortless meal from a can.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-turned kitchen gadget that cuts the lid off a can releases food within.

clue.text: Former partner works to return bonus

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: the word for works is read backwards

parts.note: works of art, as a body, are art

explanation.surface: An ex-partner's works are being sent back as a bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: Something additional on top of what is due is a bonus.

clue.text: Brave man to vex six-footer

parts.note: to gall someone is to annoy them
an insect has six legs, so an ant is a six-footer

explanation.surface: A brave man ends up annoying a very tall fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person; it is an insect with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallant is a dashing, courageous man, especially an attentive one.

clue.text: Block that is to restrict motorway progress

indicators.note: the abbreviation for 'that is' hems in the other pieces

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
M is used for British motorways, as in the M1
to pass is to move on or progress

explanation.surface: A blockage on the motorway is holding up traffic's progress.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock or blockage with no way forward is a standstill situation.

clue.text: Books to get on earlier vehicle

indicators.note: puts the verb ahead of the books

parts.note: to get on in years is to age
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone takes books along to board the earlier bus.
explanation.walkthrough: Vehicle here means a means or medium, not a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A means through which something is achieved can be called its agency or vehicle.

clue.text: Yes — Italian character receives good endorsement

indicators.note: the pieces take in the letter for good between them

parts.note: si is Italian for yes
one's nature is one's character

explanation.surface: An Italian says yes, and his good character earns approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing a document shows approval, so a name written there is an endorsement.

clue.text: Successful song provides beat

explanation.definitionFit: A popular record is a hit, and to strike is also to hit.

clue.text: One begins with pair of hips to excite crowd

definitions.text: One begins with pair of hips to excite crowd

parts.words: One begins with pair of hips to excite crowd
parts.note: the familiar chant starting 'hip hip hooray' is led by someone rousing spectators

explanation.surface: A dancer swings her hips at the start to get the crowd going.
explanation.walkthrough: The pair of hips is the double 'hip' that starts the cheer, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who leads organised chanting at a sports match rouses supporters.

clue.text: Coaster starts to manoeuvre against tide

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A coastal boat starts to manoeuvre against the tide.
explanation.walkthrough: Coaster suggests a ship; it is a drinks mat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pad placed under a glass to protect a table is a coaster.

clue.text: Noisy rabble son puts to flight

parts.note: a rout is an old word for a disorderly crowd

explanation.surface: A noisy mob chases a son away.
explanation.definitionFit: To defeat an enemy and send them fleeing in disorder is to drive them off.

clue.text: Waller got top tip from Roach — piano's inside!

parts.note: had means got or obtained

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the word Roach
takes the inner letters of piano, dropping its ends

explanation.surface: A singer called Waller picked up a top tip from someone called Roach about a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: Waller sounds like Fats Waller, but means a wall-builder: the Roman emperor behind the wall across northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor ordered the great frontier wall in Britain, so he is a builder of walls.

clue.text: It stimulates article about reformed Ireland

indicators.note: the article goes round the rearranged country

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: reformed means remade into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something stimulates a newspaper article about a reformed Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' tells you the article wraps round the country's shuffled letters, which 'reformed' signals; the drug itself is the stimulant.
explanation.definitionFit: A hormone that prepares the body for fight or flight is a stimulant.

clue.text: Polar Christmas tree stocked here

indicators.note: the tree is held within the words in front of it

explanation.surface: A Christmas tree from the polar regions is kept in stock here.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciduous conifer with needles that drop in autumn is a type of tree.

clue.text: Washington to orchestrate useless spending

parts.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state
to stage an event is to orchestrate it

explanation.surface: Washington arranges wasteful public expenditure.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss through squandering or needless spending is a synonym.

clue.text: Batsman? He's out: shame!

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the pronoun gives its letters, the 's being a link

explanation.surface: A batsman has been dismissed, and what a shame it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges BATSMAN plus HE into the answer; the cricket dismissal is surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Embarrassment or discomfiture from shame is the sense, as a noun.

clue.text: Show innermost fears, having spoken of identifying feature

parts.note: personal demons are deep-seated fears

indicators.note: signals the next word heard rather than seen

parts.note: a trait is a distinguishing characteristic

explanation.surface: Someone shows their deepest fears after speaking about a distinguishing feature.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAIT is said aloud as 'trate', the British pronunciation that rhymes with straight.
explanation.definitionFit: To show is to prove or display clearly, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Cell diagram to incorporate circle in code

indicators.note: the pieces take the circle into themselves

parts.note: a crypt is an underground chamber or cell
a graph is a diagram
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: A cell diagram includes a circle drawn in secret code.
explanation.definitionFit: Something written in cipher is a piece of code.

clue.text: Tunnel man moved, reversing

indicators.note: moved means shifted around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man in a tunnel moved and turned back.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversing is the noun-like sense of cancelling a decision or marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Cancelling or overturning a ruling makes it void, which is a reversal.

clue.text: One on phone to support communist in revolution producing pistol

indicators.note: in a down answer, the second piece sits beneath and holds up the first
the word for communist turns around

parts.note: red is a common label for a communist
a ringer is someone making a call

explanation.surface: A caller backs a communist in a revolution and produces a pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pocket handgun named after its American maker is a kind of pistol.

clue.text: Credit cards to hold out in photo

indicators.note: the words for hold out go into the photo

parts.note: pic is short for picture
to last is to endure or hold out

explanation.surface: Credit cards held up in a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment cards are made of synthetic material, so the material names them informally.

clue.text: Atone for European Pie Tax that's ridiculous

indicators.note: ridiculous means absurd, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Europe must make amends for its absurd tax on pies.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends for a wrong is to atone for it.

clue.text: Experience important as team shows

indicators.note: the word appears within the words important as team

explanation.surface: Experience is important, as the team shows.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a taste of something is to experience it briefly.

clue.text: Sensible report, for example

definitions.meaning: a report is a loud bang, an example of a noise

explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning that is solid is called sound, and a bang is a type of sound.

clue.text: Lead-free transport gets attention

indicators.note: drops the first letter, the lead, from the word

parts.note: to bear is to carry or transport

explanation.surface: Lead-free fuel for transport gets everyone's attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead-free' suggests petrol; it removes the B from BEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone your attention is to lend them your ear, an idiom.
